resources.string: Wi-Fi remote is experimental and has currently only been validated with the developer’s Sony α6700. Other camera models may behave differently.\n\nPlease report any issues by email or on GitHub. Include your camera model and your phone’s operating system and version (Android or iOS).
Live view, shutter and photo downloads
Start the camera’s smartphone Wi-Fi connection, disconnect Creators’ App, then join the camera’s Wi-Fi in phone settings. Enter the camera IP address.
Disconnected. The camera did not allow Wi-Fi shutdown; you may need to turn it off on the camera.
Disconnected. Could not confirm the Wi-Fi shutdown request. Check the camera if Wi-Fi remains on.
Capture could not be confirmed. Check the camera before taking another photo.
The camera refused the shutter request. Check its shooting mode and card.
Preview stopped. Disconnect and reconnect to try again.
Enter the camera’s IPv4 address, for example the address shown in its Wi-Fi connection details.
Join the camera’s Wi-Fi network in phone settings, then return here.
Connection permission was denied. Allow Nearby devices in the app’s permission settings, or precise Location on older Android versions, then try again.
Could not connect. Check the camera IP, keep its smartphone connection active, and close other camera-control apps.
The camera connection was lost. Join its Wi-Fi again and reconnect.
Another Wi-Fi remote session is open. Close it before connecting this camera.
Keep the camera connected by Bluetooth and close Creators’ App. Alpha GPS will start camera Wi-Fi and ask your phone to connect.
Enable the camera’s Wi-Fi over Bluetooth, then join its network in phone settings. The camera IP will be detected after you join.
Camera Wi-Fi is ready. Join the network below in phone settings, then return here and connect. If Android warns that this network has no internet, stay connected.
Approve the camera Wi-Fi connection in the system dialog…
Wait for the camera’s Bluetooth connection to finish, then try again. You can also use manual connection.
Could not start camera Wi-Fi or read its connection details. Keep the camera awake, close Creators’ App, and retry or use manual connection.
The camera accepted the Wi-Fi start command, but its connection details could not be read over Bluetooth. Retry, or join the camera’s network in phone settings and use manual connection.
Your phone could not join camera Wi-Fi or the request was declined. Retry and approve the connection, or use manual connection.
Connected to Wi-Fi but could not find the camera address. Use manual connection with the camera IP.
Turn on phone Wi-Fi, then try again.
This Android version requires phone Location to be turned on for automatic Wi-Fi joining.
Tap a photo to view and swipe through pictures. Touch and hold to select multiple photos.
Finish or cancel the download to load more photos.
Downloads matching files from the selected photos. You can choose more than one format. Files already saved in this session or exceeding the download limit are skipped.
No files available to download. They may already be saved or exceed the download limit.
Originals are saved to your photo library and stay on the camera. Keep this screen open until the download finishes.
Download original JPEG, RAW and HEIF files to your photo library. Browses card slot 1 on newer cameras. Files stay on the camera. Keep this screen open until the download finishes.
Could not read camera photos or change transfer mode. Retry, or disconnect and reconnect if the camera is busy.
No supported photos on this page.
Image exceeds the 512 MB download limit.
Download failed. Any incomplete file was removed. You can retry the download.
Download cancelled. Any incomplete file was removed.
Allow storage access to save photos to your phone.
This camera does not advertise supported photo browsing.
Downloads the HEIF and saves a full-resolution JPEG copy on this phone. HDR and some metadata may not be preserved.
Could not create a JPEG copy. This phone may not support the HEIF format or have enough memory or storage. You can download the original HEIF instead.
Allow Local Network access in the app’s Settings, then reconnect.
Connecting to camera… If iOS asks, allow Local Network access.
